thesis_triggers.event: Below ~$16.5 AT&T would trade ~5.7x NTM EBITDA on our EV (~5.2x on the peers' basis, below every incumbent except cable, Vodafone, Orange, Deutsche Telekom and Telefonica), a 6.7% dividend yield and a ~15% FCF-to-common yield: consistent only with a broken cash path (FCF well under $18B, a cut to the $24B+ buyback or dividend) or a priced national fourth carrier; the bear value is $16.42.

supervisor_summary: AT&T's research target (12m) is $23.16 (+11% from $20.93, plus a 5.3% dividend), the engine value of a driver-led set that the five revised forecasts now bracket ($22.24-24.39 after the gate arithmetic fixes, mean $23.08). The horizon EV/EBITDA stays at the post-SpaceX 6.1x, as Kilian decided; the build sits below management on 2028 (EBITDA +3.4% vs 5%+, FCF $18.5B/$20.0B vs the $19B+/$21B+ floors) because Legacy EBITDA turns negative and ARPU growth fades, while lower D&A and ~5% a year of buybacks keep 2028 EPS at $2.91, above the $2.82 floor. Our checks narrowed small gaps rather than settling a large one, so the ladder stays at the forecasters' mean; the thesis break is $16.5 (cable-like ~5.2x EBITDA). SpaceX headlines (FCC space-coverage vote Oct-29, any site deal) are the near-term risk; a 4-6% position in two tranches fits a book with no telecom exposure.
